analyst_observations: The with-skill version scores 12/12 vs baseline 11/12. The discriminating assertion is connections-with-breakage: the skill teaches the structured 'Where it breaks:' format that makes analogy limitations explicit (NAR-13 toxin line). The baseline includes implicit breakage in prose but doesn't use the structured format.

Most assertions (11/12) pass for both versions, suggesting the research brief itself and CLAUDE.md provide strong baseline context. The skill's marginal value is in format discipline (structured breakage) rather than content generation.

The with-skill version is significantly longer (1,824 words vs 1,463) and more detailed, particularly in the visual arc section. It uses ~63% more tokens and takes ~2.6x longer. The extra detail is valuable for downstream pipeline consumers (visual-spec, script-draft) but exceeds the skill's own 300-500 word target.
Both versions independently coined 'The Silicon Trap' as the named concept — strong signal that the brief's thesis is clear enough to drive concept naming without skill guidance.

Qualitative difference: the with-skill output includes Episode Format selection and Production Notes sections not present in the baseline — these are pipeline-critical decisions that the 9-decision framework ensures don't get skipped.
